response.augmented_intent: Rename all local variables representing numeric partition identifiers from "partition" to "partitionId" throughout this file and in other code locations to match the getPartitionId() API and avoid ambiguity with Partition objects; apply the same naming convention to other identifier primitives (e.g., rename user → userId, order → orderId) for clarity and consistency, while preserving the original name when the variable is an actual Partition object or when following existing method signatures.

Rename each simple-value list field (e.g. batchOperationIds, itemKeys, processInstanceKeys, state) to indicate it holds filter operations (e.g. batchOperationIdOperations, itemKeyOperations, processInstanceKeyOperations, stateOperations). Rename generic 'values' parameters and variables in builder APIs to a specific plural noun matching the element type (e.g., change 'values' to 'operations' for List<Operation<T>>). Developers should locate any method or module that handles more than one ‘intent’ variable—such as both the incoming command intent and the intent being emitted or written—and disambiguate them by renaming one to a descriptive name (e.g. ‘intentToWrite’, ‘incomingIntent’ vs. ‘outgoingIntent’, ‘userTaskIntent’ vs. ‘asyncRequestIntent’). Summarize the refactoring steps needed to migrate feature-specific request metadata into the new AsyncRequest abstraction consistently across the codebase: 1) Rename any state variable or class tied to UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata (e.g., userTaskState) to asyncRequestState (or AsyncRequestRecord/AsyncRequestState) 2) Replace all reads and writes of UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata with calls to the AsyncRequest API (append RECEIVED/PROCESSED events via stateWriter) 3) Update command and response writers to emit and handle AsyncRequest events instead of user-task-only events 4) Adjust onFinalizeCommand logic to retrieve request metadata from AsyncRequestState when metadata is missing in the command 5) Refactor tests and utilities (e.g., assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence) to expect AsyncRequest events in the intent sequence 6) Apply the same pattern to other subsystems (timer triggers, variable update flows, audit logs) by extracting their metadata handling into AsyncRequest and renaming references accordingly.

Identify every use of *Metadata (e.g., UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata) and replace it with the new AsyncRequest model: rename metadata classes and records to AsyncRequestRecord, update intent names in event emissions to AsyncRequest:RECEIVED and AsyncRequest:PROCESSED, change state lookups from recordRequestMetadata to AsyncRequestState APIs, adjust responseWriter calls to write on AsyncRequest events rather than metadata, update test utilities and assertions to assert AsyncRequest lifecycle, and remove any legacy metadata storage or methods across all affected command processors and utilities.

Apply the new AsyncRequest framework across all affected code: rename local variables (e.g., `recordRequestMetadata`) to `asyncRequest`; swap out calls to the old metadata API (`userTaskState.findRecordRequestMetadata`) for the new async request API (`asyncRequestState.findAsyncRequest` or similar); update event writing to use `AsyncRequestIntent.RECEIVED` and `AsyncRequestIntent.PROCESSED` instead of user-task-specific intents; adjust responseWriter calls to pass the generic request ID and stream ID from the AsyncRequestRecord; remove any residual references to the legacy UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata; and update tests (such as `assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence`) and other processors handling variable document or other async-triggered flows to follow the unified async request model.

Guide the second developer to generalize domain-specific property names to match the new generic enum types: rename methods and fields from setTriggerType/getTriggerType and triggerTypeProperty to setValueType/getValueType and valueTypeProperty, update all usages in declarations, constructors, serializers, and Javadoc, adjust tests and utility assertions accordingly, propagate the change across other classes referencing ValueType, and ensure backward compatibility by deprecating the old names or providing migration helpers while updating documentation and schema definitions to reflect the new naming convention.

Introduce a consistent pattern for all incident filter fields to use operation-based filters rather than simple value lists.
